medSchoolStudLife.diversity: New York Medical College believes the rich diversity of its student body and faculty is vital to its mission of educating outstanding and thoughtful health care professionals.  Diversity and inclusion are woven into the proud history of the institution and continue to be an essential component of its current-day mission.  The College seeks to admit a diverse class, including but not limited to diversity of gender, race, ethnicity, cultural and economic background, and life experience. The broad diversity of backgrounds and perspectives reflected in our community is integral to our humanistic values as a medical education institution in service to society.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: A leave of absence for good reason may be granted by the Senior Associate Dean for Medical Education. Ordinarily, a leave of absence is not granted for reason of academic difficulty.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: New York Medical College encourages its students to become engaged in activities that extend beyond the curriculum.  With over sixty clubs and organizations to choose from, students have the opportunity to participate in a wide range of academic, community service, cultural, social, and athletic activities.  Many of our students also serve on regional and national boards working on ways to improve health care. In addition to students in the School of Medicine, students from the other graduate programs at NYMC also participate in these clubs and organizations allowing for robust collaboration on events and community service projects   The College believes these outside endeavors significantly contribute to the success and well-being of its students as well as benefit the greater NYMC community.
medSchoolStudLife.setting: New York Medical College is situated on a gracious 55-acre campus in Valhalla, New York - a small suburban hamlet in Westchester County located approximately 30 miles north of New York City.  Students have the unique opportunity to be engaged in educational and student-life programs, including clinical preceptorships, community-service endeavors, cultural events, and recreational pursuits, which not only take place within our dynamic campus community but also in the geographically, racially, and socioeconomically diverse communities of Westchester County and the Lower Hudson Valley, comprising just under a million residents. Students also have easy access by car, train, or bus to New York City, one of the most dynamic and culturally diverse cities in the world.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: Most first and second-year students live on campus in apartment style residences which contributes to the strong sense of community that exists among students.  Both furnished and unfurnished on-campus housing is available.  The Housing Office also maintains a list of off-campus housing opportunities.  But residential life is more than just housing at New York Medical College. The Office of Student and Residential Life is committed to the overall growth, development, and education of students. The goal is to provide a safe, secure, comfortable environment while providing students with opportunities to become involved, share ideas, and be part of a residential community.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: New York Medical College is committed to fostering an inclusive and supportive learning environment for all students. Support systems include access to confidential counseling and wellness services, inclusive student organizations and affinity groups, mentorship opportunities with faculty and peers, and clear institutional policies that promote equity, respect, and nondiscrimination. These resources are integrated into the broader student support framework to ensure that all learners feel safe, valued, and supported throughout their medical education.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystemsForDisabilities:
The Office of Student Academic Excellence, which includes the Division of Student Academic Support and the Division of Student Accommodations and Accessibility, empowers a diverse student population in an equitable transition to graduate and medical studies. Our comprehensive services cultivate self-efficacy, resilience, and a culture of academic excellence, developing the next generation of researchers and health care leaders.

The Division of Student Accommodations and Accessibility is committed to supporting students with disabilities in accordance with applicable laws, as NYMC recognizes the importance of providing students with disabilities equitable access to the College’s facilities, programs, and services through reasonable academic adjustments, auxiliary aids and services, and reasonable modifications in practices and procedures.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms: New York Medical College and TCDM prioritize the mental health and wellness of its students through comprehensive services managed and/or provided by The Office of Student Mental Health and Wellness (SMHW). Students may access a myriad of services at no cost and with utmost attention to confidentiality. Services include psychological counseling, advocacy, psychiatric evaluation, consultation, psycho-educational events, workshops, support groups, and wellness programs. Our providers uphold the values of the office: confidentiality, professionalism, respect, empathy, and awareness with the goal of providing services and encouraging skills to enhance the quality of life and promote well-being. An individual introductory consultation is also available to discuss services and align options that best support each student during their time at NYMC.
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: Student life at NYMC offers a wide range of opportunities to join student clubs and organizations, participate in the local community, and complement your academic study with enriching activities. Campus life at NYMC means engaging recreation, and a warm, supportive environment. Learn about the different activities and resources the College offers and how you can stay physically, mentally, and spiritually healthy as you engage in a rigorous academic experience.

medSchoolCurriculum.dressCode: Appropriate attire is expected at all times as required by the educational or clinical setting.
medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms:
The Office of Student Services offers a wide-range of innovative programs to support student success.  
https://www.nymc.edu/
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Students are paired with a physician preceptor in the community beginning in the first month of school and interact with patients to develop foundational clinical and communication skills.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Lecture-based integration of basic science and clinical content along with laboratory exercises, small-group learning, self-directed study,computer-assisted instruction, and problem-based learning.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations:
3rd & 4th yr rotations/electives provide both comprehensive & specialty track training 

https://www.nymc.edu/som/education/
medSchoolCurriculum.rankStudents: Students are not numerically rank-ordered except for purposes of the Medical Student Performance Evaluation (MSPE) which places them in quintiles based on academic performance.
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: Students are expected to be present for all classes as shown on the Academic Calendar and attend all mandatory activities.  Audio and video recordings of each lecture are also available.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights: Offering a breadth of foundational science and clinical training, the curriculum provides students an integrated four-year progression of knowledge and skills. Educational hallmarks include a collaborative student community; engaged and accessible faculty; early and regular patient encounters under the direct supervision of a community physician preceptor in first and second year; on-site state-of-the-art standardized patient and simulation programs all four years specifically tailored towards refinement of individual clinical and communication skills; third-year clerkship rotations at a wide-range of clinical affiliated sites located throughout the tri-state area; specialty tracks in the fourth-year to allow students to align their electives within their area of specialty interest.  Additional areas of concentration are available to fourth-year students to develop expertise in non-clinical aspects of professional practice.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: New York Medical College believes a strong foundation in the tenants of primary care prepares its graduates for success in any field of medicine they choose.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: Basic science, translational, and clinical research opportunities are available through the NYMC Graduate School of Basic Medical Sciences, our clinical partners at neighboring Westchester Medical Center and the Maria Fareri Children's Hospital as well as the broad network of hospitals and research institutions throughout our catchment area in the tri-state (NY/NJ/CT) region.
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: Although not required, NYMC students are actively engaged and assume leadership positions in a myriad of service-oriented activities that benefit the college and greater community.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: Although research is not required, a majority of students research either on campus or at sites throughout NY-metro area.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation:
New York Medical College (NYMC) is a graduate health science institution situated on a gracious suburban campus in Westchester County, approximately 30 miles north of New York City.  The College educates graduate students for careers in medicine, bio-medical sciences, public health, and the allied health professions through its School of Medicine, Graduate School of Basic Medical Sciences, and School of Health Sciences and Practice.  

Founded in 1860, the NYMC School of Medicine is one of the oldest and largest medical schools in the country, and has grown in size and stature over the past century and a half. Today it is comprised of more than 800 medical students, 2,800  faculty, and offers four degrees:  MD, MD/MPH, MD/PhD, and an MS in Medical Ethics, and is lauded for the clinical training of its graduates.

NYMC is a member of the Touro University System - one of the largest biomedical higher education consortium under one institutional banner in the United States.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement: New York Medical College is a graduate health sciences university whose purpose is to educate physicians, scientists, public health specialists, and other healthcare professionals, and to conduct biomedical and population-based research. Through its faculty and affiliated clinical partners, the College provides service to its community in an atmosphere of excellence, scholarship, and professionalism. New York Medical College believes the rich diversity of its student body and faculty is important to its mission of educating outstanding health care professionals for the multicultural world of the 21st century. This commitment to diversity and inclusion is woven into the fabric of the institution.  Students come from across the US, representing a broad range of racial, ethnic, cultural, economic, and educational backgrounds.

medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
As we conduct complete holistic review of applications, we encourage you to submit your AMCAS application if all other elements of your application are complete while you wait for your MCAT score to be available. You will have the opportunity to alert us of your new test date and you will receive a holistic review once your MCAT score is available to us. Secondary applications must be fully complete including MCAT score and supplemental application by January 31st.

It is the policy of the NYMC School of Medicine to seek to admit a diverse class with respect to gender, cultural, and economic background and life experience.  The School believes a diverse student body provides a valuable educational experience that prepares its medical students for the real world of medical practice in a multicultural society.

The Committee on Admissions has the difficult task of selecting an entering class from thousands of applicants. There are many more applicants who meet the qualifications for the study of medicine than can be admitted to an incoming class. Each applicant is subject to an individualized holistic review  - defined by the AAMC as a process of assessing an applicant’s capabilities by which balanced consideration is given to foundational experiences, personal attributes and academic metrics and, when considered in combination, how the individual might contribute value as a medical student and physician. 

The Committee strives to select those candidates who demonstrate proficiency in the Core Competencies for Entering Medical Students that have been endorsed by the AAMC Group of Student Affairs (GSA) and Committee on Admissions (COA).  These competencies fall into four categories: (1) Interpersonal; (2) Intrapersonal; (3) Thinking and Reasoning; and (4) Science.  The Committee believes these foundational competencies are essential for success in medical school and future professional practice. 

As a future medical student candidates should have a college education that includes premedical science coursework required for medical school as well as a broad exposure to the humanities and social sciences. Academic competence to succeed in medical school is assessed by the applicant’s college record including GPA and MCAT scores.

An applicant must also demonstrate excellent observation and communication skills as well as the motor function and conceptual, integrative and quantitative skills required for the study of medicine. As a future physician, an applicant must have the physical capacity and emotional maturity to complete medical school and practice medicine independently. These skills are outlined in the NYMC School of Medicine Technical Standards for Admissions and Continued Enrollment.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid:
The Board of Trustees determines the annual tuition rate for the School of Medicine.

NYMC tuition-scholarships are available. 

The NYMC Office of Student Financial Planning is lauded for the comprehensive loan and debt management counseling it provides all students prior to matriculation, throughout medical school as well as after graduation.   New York Medical College graduates have one of the lowest student loan default rates in the nation.
medSchoolFinancial.tuitionPolicy: There is a NYMC School of Medicine tuition refund policy for all students who terminate their medical college registration by official leave of absence or withdrawal. Students who receive federal student aid are also subject to  a separate Federal Title IV Funds Refund Policy.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec:
Applicants must have successfully completed the following of premed requirements (or have them in progress) from an accredited college in the United States or Canada:

General Biology, 2 semesters or equivalent, with labs 
General Chemistry, 2 semesters or equivalent, with labs 
Organic Chemistry, 1st semester or equivalent with lab
Biochemistry, 1 semester or equivalent, (with or without lab) 
Physics, 2 semesters or equivalent, with labs 
English, 2 semesters or equivalent (or successful completion of the English requirements of your undergraduate institution)

Applicants are also expected to meet posted Technical Standards for Admission and Enrollment. https://www.nymc.edu/som/about/policies/
medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: It is highly recommended that Prerequisite coursework be taken within the last 10 years.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors:
Candidates for admission to the School of Medicine must have a broad educational background and possess the intelligence, integrity and personal and emotional characteristics necessary to become effective physicians. They must meet the School's admissions requirements and show evidence of the capacity to successfully complete the rigorous course of study in medical school.

Each applicant is subject to an individualized, balanced holistic review as defined by the AAMC.  The committee on admissions strives to select those candidates who demonstrate proficiency in the core competencies the School of Medicine believes are essential for success in medical school and professional practice. These include but are not limited to the published AAMC Core Competencies for Entering Medical Students.  https://www.aamc.org/competencies
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: The SOM Committee on Admissions views shadowing as an activity that provides applicants a basic introduction to medicine.  Applicants to NYMC are strongly encouraged to pursue additional clinical experiences that extend beyond shadowing for which they have appropriate clinical training.  This applies to international clinical experiences as well as those which take place in the United States.
